3. The defendant, on the other hand, filed written statement denying the contention of the plaintiff on material particulars. They stated in their written statement that the suit dag was the bhiti land situated in Karimgonj Bazar and there were 5 bhitis. On the death of the owner Abdur Rahman his sons and daughters made amicable partition and Ismail Bepari got 0.1/2 decimals of land and Ibrahim and Ahmed got the remaining 0.1/2 decimals of land. Israil Bepari got no share in the said dag and in exchange of his claim Israil got some bhiti land. On the southern portion of the suit land dag No. 2012 measuring 0.1 decimals stands which is owned and possessed by the defendant on taking pattani from the original owner on 12th Bhadra, 1351 BS and on the death of Ismail the plaintiff got 0.1/2 decimals of land. Wahed, Ahmed and Ibrahim constructed the house ejmali along with the defendant. The defendant No.1 purchased 0.1/2 decimals of land on 29-8-81 by a kabala from the heirs of Wahed but the defendant did not get any possession of the same. This defendant was never a tenant under the plaintiff and this defendant is in possession of the suit land by virtue of his own right. The plaintiff out of greed filed the false suit and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 4. The learned Small Cause Courts Act Judge found-that Israil Bepari by purchase got his share in the suit land and he sold his share in favour of the plaintiff No. 1 and he rented one kotha in favour of the defendant but the defendant stopped payment of rent and, as such, the plaintiff filed the suit for ejectment but the defendant has raised the Claim that he did never take the Kotha on rent but he took pattan from the superior landlord. The defendant also stated that the suit kotha is not situated on dag No. 2021 but the same appertains to dag No. 2012 and he has further stated that Israil Bepari did not get share in the suit property. The learned Judge has observed that on the pleadings of both the parties it appears that there is a serious question of title involved in this Small Cause Courts Act proceeding. As the suit is a Small Cause Courts Act suit there is hardly any scope to go in details on question of title. Then the learned Judge went into the question of title and has decided the same. Although he has observed that in a Small Cause Courts Act suit there is no scope to decide the question of title elaborately but abruptly came to the finding that in suit dag No. 2021 the defendant has absolutely no title and as such, he is evictable from the suit dag. He found that Ibrahim and Israil got 0.01 decimals of land Ext. A which they have purchased from Ullah  Bepari on 11-10-64. By a sale deed dated 10-3-65 Ibrahim Bepari sold his share in favour of the plaintiff. The learned Judge came to the finding that the plaintiffs in this way have acquired title to the extent of 0.3/4 decimals in dag No. 2021. In this way the learned SCC Judge decided the title in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit land. The learned Judge simply said that by oral evidence the plaintiff proved that the defendant has got no title in the suit property at all but he did not discuss the evidence. The learned Judge has also observed that the defendant is a tenant under the plaintiff. Although DW 3 stated in his cross-examination that he does not know whether the defendant is a tenant or not under the plaintiff. The learned judge has also observed that the defendant did not adduce any evidence in order to prove the tenancy although onus heavily lies on the plaintiff to prove whether the defendant is his tenant or not. DW 2 stated in his cross-examination that he cannot say in which kotha the defendant has taken the bhara. Although DW 4 has stated that Israil Bepari has no share in the suit premises, the learned Judge then abruptly came to the conclusion that defendant is the tenant under the plaintiff in the said kotha. Accordingly, the learned Small Cause Courts Act Judge found that the plaintiff is entitled to get the decree for eviction of the defendant and he decreed the suit.
